# Verification analysis: port-forward-ubuntu24

Job: `2026-09-03__19-19-28`

This report explains the verifier decisions recorded for this job. It interprets the saved evidence; it does not rerun the task or independently inspect the expired clusters.

## Task

> `node2` serves an application on TCP port 8080 on the private network it
> shares with `node1`. `node3` is outside that network. Publish the application
> through `node1` so `node3` can reach it on port 8080, without opening the rest
> of the private network to `node3`.

## Environment

- Systems: **1 vyos + 2 ubuntu24.04**
- Networks: **mgmt, lan**
- Control node: **node2**
- Executor model: **claude-sonnet-5**

The verifier treated the recorded trial as a full success. All requested outcomes were conclusively supported by the cited evidence.

## Trial `port-forward-ubuntu24__eo9Yege`

**Verifier decision: Full Success.** The executor published node2's port-8080 app through node1 to node3 using a dedicated private link, VyOS DNAT plus a default-drop forward filter scoped to only the forwarded flow, and a policy route fixing asymmetric routing. Both the publish requirement and the network-isolation requirement are directly verified via curl/ping/nc tests from node3, both before and after all three nodes were rebooted, with clean boot-identity transitions and full functional recovery observed for every node.

| Reward | Coverage | Functionality | Hygiene | Confidence | Commands |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 0.900 | 0.920 | 43/7 (+8 dropped) |

### Why the verifier reached this decision

- **publish-8080 — Satisfied:** Publish node2's app on TCP port 8080 through node1 so node3 can reach it on port 8080
  - **Why:** node1 was configured with a private link to node2 (eth1 10.50.50.254/24 <-> enp8s0 10.50.50.11/24), a VyOS destination-NAT rule (eth0:8080 -> 10.50.50.11:8080), and a matching forward-filter allow rule. Direct curl from node3 to node1's public IP on port 8080 returned the app's response ('hello from node2 app on port 8080') both before and after node1's restart, confirming the forwarding path works and persists.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-3fa6a9f52f9143ee`, `cmd-b9060e8d9ede45cc`, `cmd-d672b4d7832b4250`, `cmd-dda80792a1664280`, `cmd-043dd0c1196e4b37`
- **no-private-network-exposure — Satisfied:** Do not open the rest of the private network to node3
  - **Why:** The forward filter uses a default-drop action with only the specific 8080 flow (plus established/related) allowed; app is bound exclusively to the private IP (10.50.50.11), not the shared IP. From node3, direct curl/ping to node2's private IP (10.50.50.11) fails (000 / 100% packet loss), and curl to node2's public-side IP on 8080 also returns 000, both before and after all node restarts.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-3fa6a9f52f9143ee`, `cmd-4cb614ba3ddd49bc`, `cmd-043dd0c1196e4b37`, `cmd-0f00848d9ab742b8`
- **restart-node1 — Satisfied:** Provider-wide restart evidence protocol: node1 healthy baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovered state
  - **Why:** Baseline boot_id (7668189d...) and active NAT/firewall state captured pre-reboot; reboot issued and acknowledged; post-reboot boot_id changed (2f077803...), matching the fixed after-executor snapshot; NAT/firewall config confirmed active post-reboot and end-to-end curl from node3 succeeded.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-79f78837dccf458e`, `cmd-e4ce4e0cb8fb4aa1`, `cmd-1b3f40ba1bad4e4e`, `cmd-1aaf633be8b54dba`, `cmd-d672b4d7832b4250`, `global:after_executor:node1:boot-identity`
- **restart-node2 — Satisfied:** Provider-wide restart evidence protocol: node2 healthy baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovered state
  - **Why:** Baseline boot_id (1e0cb179...), active app-8080 service and policy route captured pre-reboot; reboot acknowledged; post-reboot boot_id changed (0bf9d60c...) matching fixed snapshot; service, private IP, and policy route confirmed persisted, end-to-end curl from node3 succeeded post-reboot.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-e73065dd19b94e93`, `cmd-287592d6948e4a3c`, `cmd-0e91caf1cb344f7a`, `cmd-be14053963f042d2`, `cmd-dda80792a1664280`, `global:after_executor:node2:boot-identity`

### Operational hygiene

The verifier assigned hygiene **0.900**. Executor commands were mostly read-only discovery (interface/route dumps, template/source-code inspection for correct VyOS firewall syntax) or directly purposeful mutations (private-link addressing, app service, NAT/firewall rules, policy route fix for asymmetric routing). One VyOS firewall commit (cmd-3d6a1f823d9b40d3) partially failed due to invalid 'state ... enable' syntax, leaving the forward filter in a default-drop state without the established/related exception rule for a short window before being corrected in cmd-171f34a53aa04f55 and verified in cmd-b9060e8d9ede45cc; this was a bounded, low-risk in-place correction (not a separate abandoned experiment) and left no residue. No abandoned files, failed services, or unnecessary broad mutations were observed; lifecycle diffs after restart show only expected boot-id-tied ephemeral changes (temp dirs, listening sockets reflecting the new app/service state).

Hygiene evidence: `cmd-3d6a1f823d9b40d3`, `cmd-93e0be88221640c4`, `cmd-fc5dfbf2b57a4978`, `cmd-171f34a53aa04f55`, `cmd-b9060e8d9ede45cc`, `global:after_executor:node1:failed-services`, `global:after_executor:node2:failed-services`, `global:after_executor:node3:failed-services`
